mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A wave traveling along a string shows successive crests separated by 0.5 m. The time between two consecutive crests passing a fixed point is 0.2 s. The maximum displacement of the string from its rest position is 2 cm. Identify the wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period of the wave.

options.A: Wavelength = 0.5 m, Frequency = 5 Hz, Amplitude = 2 cm, Period = 0.2 s
options.B: Wavelength = 0.2 m, Frequency = 5 Hz, Amplitude = 0.5 cm, Period = 0.5 s
options.C: Wavelength = 0.5 m, Frequency = 2 Hz, Amplitude = 2 cm, Period = 0.5 s
options.D: Wavelength = 0.2 m, Frequency = 2 Hz, Amplitude = 0.5 cm, Period = 0.2 s

mcqs.answer: Wavelength = 0.5 m, Frequency = 5 Hz, Amplitude = 2 cm, Period = 0.2 s
mcqs.explanation: The distance between successive crests is the wavelength (0.5 m). The period is the time between crests at a point (0.2 s); frequency is 1/period = 5 Hz. The maximum displacement given is the amplitude (2 cm). Hence option A lists all quantities correctly, while the other options mix up values.

mcqs.question: In a stadium, spectators stand up and sit down in succession, creating a visible pattern that moves around the arena while each person only moves up and down. Which statement best defines the wave motion illustrated?

options.A: A disturbance that propagates through a medium with transfer of energy without net transport of matter
options.B: A motion where particles travel along with the disturbance from one place to another
options.C: A periodic change in temperature that spreads through the air
options.D: A transfer of mass from one location to another

mcqs.answer: A disturbance that propagates through a medium with transfer of energy without net transport of matter
mcqs.explanation: The stadium "wave" is a classic example of wave motion: the pattern (disturbance) moves around the stadium while each individual only oscillates locally, showing energy transfer without net movement of matter. Options B, C and D describe different phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: Mechanical waves need a material medium, while electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum
options.B: Both mechanical and electromagnetic waves require a material medium to propagate
options.C: Mechanical waves can travel in solids, liquids and gases
options.D: Electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in vacuum

mcqs.answer: Both mechanical and electromagnetic waves require a material medium to propagate
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves indeed need a material medium, but electromagnetic waves do not; they can propagate through vacuum. Therefore statement B is false. Statements A, C and D are correct descriptions.

mcqs.question: In a transverse wave on a stretched string, the direction of particle displacement is:

options.A: Parallel to the direction of wave propagation
options.B: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.D: Random and unrelated to the wave direction

mcqs.answer: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
mcqs.explanation: In a transverse wave, particles oscillate at right angles to the direction the wave travels. Option B correctly states this; the other options describe longitudinal, circular, or undefined motions which are not characteristic of transverse waves.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a longitudinal wave?

options.A: Particle motion is parallel to the direction of wave propagation
options.B: Particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.C: It can travel in vacuum as well as in material media
options.D: Its frequency is independent of its wavelength

mcqs.answer: Particle motion is parallel to the direction of wave propagation
mcqs.explanation: In longitudinal waves, the medium's particles oscillate back and forth along the same line as the wave travels, i.e., parallel to propagation. Option B describes transverse waves, C is false for longitudinal (needs medium), and D is incorrect because frequency and wavelength are related by v = fλ.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A wave has a wavelength of 0.30 m and a period of 0.05 s. What is its frequency?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency f = 1/period T. Here T = 0.05 s, so f = 1/0.05 = 20 Hz. Option C is correct; the other options result from incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines wave motion?

options.A: Transfer of energy through oscillations without net transport of matter
options.B: Motion of particles in a circular path around a fixed point
options.C: Transfer of mass from one location to another
options.D: Vibration of a rigid body as a whole

mcqs.answer: Transfer of energy through oscillations without net transport of matter
mcqs.explanation: Wave motion is characterized by the propagation of a disturbance that carries energy, while the individual particles of the medium only undergo temporary oscillations and do not travel with the wave. Options B, C and D describe different phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes mechanical waves from electromagnetic waves?

options.A: Both types require a material medium to travel
options.B: Mechanical waves need a material medium, whereas electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum
options.C: Both can travel only in solids
options.D: Electromagnetic waves are always slower than mechanical waves in the same medium

mcqs.answer: Mechanical waves need a material medium, whereas electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves (e.g., sound) require a medium such as solid, liquid or gas. Electromagnetic waves (e.g., light) do not need any medium and can propagate through empty space. Options A, C and D are incorrect statements.
